questions.question:
Identify the correct sentence with inversion for emphasis.

A) Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
B) Only after the storm passed did the children go out to play.
C) It was not until midnight that the power finally returned.
D) So fast did the car go that it almost hit the tree.
options: Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
Only after the storm passed did the children go out to play.
It was not until midnight that the power finally returned.
So fast did the car go that it almost hit the tree.
questions.answer: Only after the storm passed did the children go out to play.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses a cleft sentence to highlight specific information?

A) It was John who broke the window yesterday.
B) John, not Peter, broke the window yesterday.
C) That John broke the window yesterday is clear.
D) John broke the window yesterday, as opposed to Peter.
options: It was John who broke the window yesterday.
John, not Peter, broke the window yesterday.
That John broke the window yesterday is clear.
John broke the window yesterday, as opposed to Peter.
questions.answer: It was John who broke the window yesterday.

questions.question:
Select the correct form of the conditional sentence.

A) If I were you, I would have taken the job.
B) If I had been you, I would have taken the job.
C) If I was you, I would have taken the job.
D) If I had been, I would have taken the job.
options: If I were you, I would have taken the job.
If I had been you, I would have taken the job.
If I was you, I would have taken the job.
If I had been, I would have taken the job.
questions.answer: If I were you, I would have taken the job.

questions.question:
Which option correctly uses the subjunctive mood?

A) I suggest that he goes to the doctor.
B) I suggest that he go to the doctor.
C) I suggest that he should go to the doctor.
D) I suggest that he is going to the doctor.
options: I suggest that he goes to the doctor.
I suggest that he go to the doctor.
I suggest that he should go to the doctor.
I suggest that he is going to the doctor.
questions.answer: I suggest that he go to the doctor.

questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly employs ellipsis to avoid repetition.

A) She doesn't like coffee, but she does like tea.
B) She doesn't like coffee, but likes tea.
C) She doesn't like coffee, but she likes tea.
D) She doesn't like coffee, but she is liking tea.
options: She doesn't like coffee, but she does like tea.
She doesn't like coffee, but likes tea.
She doesn't like coffee, but she likes tea.
She doesn't like coffee, but she is liking tea.
questions.answer: She doesn't like coffee, but likes tea.
